whg-cardone-public-arrow.citation: Woods Hole Group (2024), EddyWatch circulation chart explicitly labeling Eddy Cardone; original provider image reproduced by WLRN in How an eddy in the Gulf of Mexico could supercharge hurricanes in a busy season, published 27 May 2024.
whg-cardone-public-arrow.access: Original public 1988 × 1530 provider chart acquired from the image linked by WLRN; SHA-verified and actual pixels reviewed. Visible Woods Hole Group / EddyWatch credit and EDDY CARDONE label. No observation date printed. Four black-ink extrema verified on one idle local CPU; closed-ink tests rejected and no gaps repaired.

records.source_locator: Original Woods Hole Group / EddyWatch image linked by WLRN, published 27 May 2024. EDDY CARDONE appears beside the black circulation arrows. No observation date or arrow contour threshold is printed.
records.definition: Geographic east–west bounding span of the plotted Cardone black circulation arrows, using four isolated native-ink extremum windows.
records.scope: Provider circulation-arrow illustration only, not a measured physical outer boundary, closed contour, diameter or principal width.
records.qualification: Four native-ink extremum windows exclude coloured drifter tracks and text. Black arrows fail both closed-ink tests; no gaps are joined or repaired. Six pixels per extremum, ±2 pixels on six grid anchors, 64 axis scenarios and outward 25 km reporting describe reading/axis sensitivity only. Physical extent, map projection distortion and field/product error remain unquantified. The chart has no observation date: 27 May 2024 is publication context only, and the screenshot filename is not a sample timestamp. No current threshold, exact center, radius, diameter, area, footprint, state join, rank or seasonal envelope inferred.
